subject.title: [Feature]: Auto-discovery of agent configurations from external workspaces

question: Should OpenClaw add core trusted workspace-agent discovery, or keep agent registration explicit through existing config/RPC/CLI workflows?
rationale: The request adds new config, filesystem scanning, trust boundaries, precedence, and live routing semantics that source inspection cannot safely decide without maintainer product/security intent.

options.title: Keep Explicit Registration
options.body: Continue using central config plus `agents.create/update/delete` and CLI registration, and leave external discovery to operator tooling unless a smaller missing API is identified.

options.title: Design Trusted Discovery
options.body: Define a core discovery contract with trusted roots, file patterns, precedence, validation, reload/watch semantics, and security proof before implementation.

options.title: Focus On Zero-Restart Registration
options.body: Treat the user pain as runtime agent registration/reload ergonomics and improve explicit add/update flows without glob-based config discovery.

recommendation.title: Keep Explicit Registration
recommendation.body: Continue using central config plus `agents.create/update/delete` and CLI registration, and leave external discovery to operator tooling unless a smaller missing API is identified.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest current history signal across the agent config, command, and gateway management boundaries involved in the product decision.
